title: 28th sitting of the 20th Majlis
presiding: Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Speaker); Deputy Speaker Ahmed Saleem chaired part of the Foreign Investment Bill debate
summary: The sitting opened at 9:01 with 51 members present, approved the minutes of sittings 22 to 24, and spent the question session on the Minister of Sports, Fitness and Recreation, who answered members' questions on football and futsal grounds, floodlights, turf and youth centres in many islands. The removal case of Prosecutor General Hussain Shameem was read out and sent to the Judiciary Committee, the Urban Development Bill had its first reading, and the preliminary debate on the Foreign Investment Bill began, with supportive speeches, concerns about provisions, and sharp exchanges over politics and investor trust. This part ends mid-speech in the debate. Some text in this part is garbled by the PDF layer but the flow is readable. The debate on the Foreign Investment bill finished, with members from both sides discussing investor protection, how investment approvals work and whether the bill is detailed enough. Debate on two related government bills then followed: one amending the Business Registration Act (foreign parties must register a company or partnership and get investment approval) and one amending the Financial Securities Act (letting foreign parties invest in securities). After a recess all three bills were voted on and passed their first stage without opposition, and each was sent to the Economic Committee. The text of this part is partly garbled, so some speech details are approximate.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau (Minister of Sports, Fitness and Recreation)
positions: Kendhoo floodlight works are scheduled to be awarded in the fourth quarter; the handball court is delayed by a land and site issue.
Many projects were inherited and the combined cost exceeds a year's budget, so he said they would prioritise with councils and often fund projects in stages.
He asked members to budget at least half of a project's value so works can finish within two years, and promised updates to several members.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked when a futsal pitch and handball court will be built in Kendhoo, and for updates on football grounds in Dhonfanu, Kihadhoo and Kamadhoo.
In the debate, said the bill was first brought by the previous government and warned that political unrest and boycotts can scare off investors.
Raised concern that land can be fully owned by foreigners, which he said conflicts with the Constitution.
Said section 12 on approval is very detailed while sector definitions are thin, suggested aligning with the international industrial classification, and worried other laws could curb investor rights.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked whether any sports work had been done in the seven Addu islands since the government took office.
In the debate, argued that political history, including the GMR dispute and the 'India Out' campaign, shapes investor confidence.
Raised concerns about provisions on the state taking over investments and on firms becoming fully foreign-owned.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked for updates on floodlights at the Maafaru and Manadhoo football grounds and on the Manadhoo indoor sports complex.
In the debate, called the bill important for the economy and said the outdated 1979 law leaves investors without enough legal protection.
Supported the amendment, saying it opens securities investment to foreign parties and gives investors legal protection and certainty.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked when a futsal pitch will be built in Galolhu.
In the debate, said the bill removed the requirement for foreign contractors to register and that its objectives do not state investor protection clearly.
Said the mention of the state taking over investments in the bill's opening section sends a negative message to investors.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked when work starts on the Feydhoo handball court and the Kanditheemu and Bileddhoo youth centres.
In the debate, called the bill good in itself but said investor trust has been damaged by political actions and by members' conduct in the chamber.
Raised concern about the national-interest and national-security considerations in section 15(b) of the bill.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Introduced the Foreign Investment Bill, saying Maldives needs diversified investment and ranks 144 of 190 in ease of doing business.
Said the bill sets investable sectors, licensing, investor protections and state-taking rules, and asked committee experts to improve it.
As the bill's sponsor, replied that states limit foreign investment in sensitive sectors, that approval stages are set by the ministry, and asked the committee to move quickly.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Supported the bill, saying the 1979 law is outdated and the new bill creates a modern, investor-friendly business environment.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill as policy-linked and hoped investment would reach northern Miladhunmadulu, which he said has been left out of foreign investment.
Supported the bill, arguing registration of foreign businesses improves monitoring, transparency and compliance and reduces financial crime.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Raised two points of order about remarks made about another member's family and said such personal comments breach the rules of debate.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Introduced the Business Registration amendment: foreign parties register a company or partnership and obtain investment approval, with a securities exception capped at 10 percent ownership per transaction.
In closing, asked for the bill to be passed quickly in committee.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked about progress on lights and a handball court at Filladhoo ground, and when floodlights will be installed at the Kela football ground.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked when work will start on a futsal ground in Fuvahmulah's Funadhu area, saying the city council had worked to stop it.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Asked how the ministry will resolve projects listed in the budget without enough funding and how it would handle this in the next budget.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked when work on the Fehendhoo football ground will begin, since it was budgeted.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked when floodlights at Maradhoo football ground and work on the Maradhoo youth centre will begin.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Asked when work on Nilandhoo futsal ground will restart and when the damaged turf at Kondey football ground will be replaced.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Asked whether Male' football grounds were given to specific groups, whether Hulhumale' has plans for a large ground, and how night-time play and noise complaints will be handled.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked when turf laying will begin at Vaikaradhoo ground now that the sub-base is finished.

speakers.name: Ali Ashrag
positions: Asked when work on the Kinbidhoo and Vandhoo futsal grounds will start, noting Kinbidhoo has no football or futsal ground.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Asked when the stalled Isdhoo youth centre, about 75 percent complete, will be finished.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked what sports work can be done in 2024 in Maavashu, Kunahandhoo and Hithadhoo and for an update on works under way.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Asked when turf work at Maduvvari football ground and the stalled youth centre will resume.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked about Rasdhoo ground lights, the Rasdhoo sports complex, and why Ukulhas ground turf is still not laid after about three years.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said foreign investment brings jobs and income, asked whether foreign money will flow through Maldivian banks given the dollar shortage, and raised foreigners entering small local businesses.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the bill as protecting local and foreign investors, citing past share sales and said some past opposition actions harmed investment.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Thanked the sponsors and said tourism dominates the economy, so political boycotts of tourism harm investor confidence; speech continues in the next part.
Closing part of a speech begun in the previous part: urged that investor safety and a good example to the world be priorities, and that parties not harm tourism for political aims.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the bill, said small businesses struggle to raise capital, and called for a stronger banking system with lower lending rates and for better laws for investors.

speakers.name: Mohamed Afoo Hamid
positions: Introduced the Financial Securities amendment to let foreign parties invest in securities, linking it to the other two bills and citing limited capital market activity in 2023.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 22, 23 and 24 of 2024 were accepted because no member submitted amendments.
The chair had no announcements for the sitting.
The case to remove Prosecutor General Hussain Shameem was sent to the Judiciary Committee under rule 129(a).
The Urban Development Bill had its first reading.
Preliminary debate on the Foreign Investment Bill opened and was still going at the end of this part.
Foreign Investment bill accepted and sent to the Economic Committee for study.
Business Registration Act amendment bill accepted and sent to the Economic Committee for study.
Financial Securities Act amendment bill accepted and sent to the Economic Committee for study.
Committee meetings for the day announced; the sitting adjourned until Thursday 15 August 2024 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept the Foreign Investment bill (sponsor: Central Hithadhoo)
Accept the bill amending the Business Registration Act, 18/2014 (sponsor: Faresmaathodaa)
Accept the bill amending the Financial Securities Act, 2/2006 (sponsor: Kendhikulhudhoo)
